name: PA-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Summer Lee holds a roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage over James Hayes
District leans Democratic by about 10 points and Lee is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Lee near 98 percent to win
No general-election polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: Lee combines a D+10 district, incumbency, and a near-total fundraising dominance over Hayes, who has raised about $40,000 with under $10,000 on hand; markets price her at 98 percent and nothing in the record suggests competition.
model.watch: A last-minute wave of outside spending against Lee or an extreme national Republican swing could narrow the margin, though closing a twenty-point gap would be historic.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Summer Lee enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a Pittsburgh-area district that leans about ten points Democratic at the presidential level. She has raised roughly $1.5 million and holds more than $1.6 million on hand, while Republican James Hayes has raised about $40,000 with under $10,000 remaining, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters. No independent general-election polling is available for this contest.

Prediction markets put Lee's chances near 98 percent, and no race raters have flagged the seat as competitive. The main uncertainties are the absence of polling and the possibility of an unusually strong national Republican environment, but even a sizable shift would need to be historic to erase a twenty-point structural advantage. The evidence points to a solidly Democratic seat.
